title: 🎭 Characters, Families & Relationships
rawNotionMarkup: This page is the reference for established characters in Eryndor, their biographies, personalities, relationships, occupations, knowledge boundaries and current commitments. Dated actions and scene-by-scene developments belong in the separate Campaign Chronicle; this page should be updated only when campaign events establish durable character facts. ## Character canon rules - NPCs are autonomous people with their own goals, responsibilities, loyalties, relationships, limitations and lives. - NPCs only know information they have been told, personally witnessed, read in an accessible source or could reasonably discover. - Do not give a character secret knowledge merely because it would make a scene easier. - A character's species or cultural reputation is not a substitute for an individual personality. - Preserve ages, names, relationships, occupations and established history. Do not silently reconcile contradictions. - Gloin's actions, words, thoughts and intentions are controlled by the player. Never write unchosen dialogue or actions for him. - Characters can disagree, refuse, make mistakes, conceal information, change their minds, be injured or die when events warrant it. No NPC has guaranteed plot protection. ## Gloin Hammerfeld - People: Khazari dwarf. - Age: 42. - Origin: Common-born, from Karak-Varn. - Occupation: Currently unemployed; pursuing training and opportunities. - Military status: Not enlisted. - Ancestry: Unknown and intentionally unresolved. No hidden lineage, chosen-one status or predetermined destiny. - Character path: Open. Gloin may pursue combat, runesmithing, engineering, trade, exploration, politics or another path through his choices and earned progress. ### Personality and established character Gloin is outgoing and curious, increasingly courageous, ambitious without being self-assured, practical and interested in learning. He values family and humour. His confidence and abilities develop through experience; he is not automatically an expert or a legendary hero. ### Current skills and development - Beginner in combat, with no prior experience striking a person with an axe. - Accepted into Sergeant Keldrun's six-week civilian shield-and-axe course, three sessions per week. - Preliminary Deepcraft and Runecraft potential; possible Stonecalling affinity, not mastery. - Learning First Throne script. Three introductory symbols in active practice: Hold, Within and Until Command. Do not claim he has learned twelve symbols. - Beginning engineering fundamentals with Borin Ashmantle. - Developing practical Deepcraft perception through supervised exercises with Maela. His impressions are preliminary and do not prove conscious communication with stone or a reliable Stonecalling ability. - Has not yet activated a rune himself. Maela has demonstrated a basic modern Khazari warming rune. ### Earlier controlled aptitude tests Maela's preliminary assessment recorded: - Strong potential in Deepcraft. - Strong potential in Runecraft. - Possible affinity for Stonecalling. - Forgebinding, Hearthmagic and Ancestral Binding had not been tested. During earlier controlled tests, Gloin felt a vibration like a distant heartbeat from an ancient rune, identified a cold section in a broken rune, and briefly elicited a glow from a disconnected binding stone. Maela stopped before overstressing an untrained resonance. These were preliminary signs of aptitude, not mastery or proof of a fully developed supernatural ability. Further Stonecalling tests require a proper grounding stone and controlled conditions. Gloin should not attempt uncontrolled magical experiments. Maela's broad estimate for learning runesmithing was that basic usefulness may take a few years, dependable skill around a decade, and accomplishment several decades. This is her professional estimate, not a guaranteed timetable for Gloin. ### Last confirmed condition and resources The following is the last confirmed status at the campaign pause; update only when events occur. - Healthy and uninjured. - Wealth: 10 silver crowns and 82 copper pieces at the last confirmed balance. - Currency now has four standard denominations: 100 copper = 1 silver; 100 silver = 1 gold; 100 gold = 1 platinum. Gloin's existing ledger remains in silver and copper unless a transaction makes conversion necessary. - Inventory: ordinary clothes; leather boots with worn soles; personal axe; family keepsake (its significance is not established); borrowed copy of The Foundations of First Throne Script; notebook containing notes and survey-symbol sketches. - Borin retains the original partial survey. Gloin does not possess it. - Maela has not yet provided the name or route of the quarry that supplied her workshop granite. She agreed to retrieve old supplier records. ### Commitments and scheduled training - Maela Deepforge: Provisional runesmithing apprenticeship at the Silver Anvil, twice weekly when schedules permit. First month carries no immediate fee. Curriculum includes First Throne script, modern Khazari runic fundamentals, identifying active and dormant enchantments, magical materials and controlled practical activation. - Sergeant Keldrun Broadshield: Six-week civilian shield-and-axe course, three sessions weekly. Initial assessment: good instinct for redirecting pushes, footwork needs refinement, axe control fair, no combat experience and good discipline. Day 22's session was excused for the mine inspection. Next planned session Day 23 morning; exact time not established. - Bruni Hammerfeld: Metallurgy lesson at 11:30 AM on Autumn Day 23. Bring notebook, work clothes and gloves. First topic: ores, refining and distinguishing good stock from poor material. - Elska Hammerfeld: Discreet research into historical attempts to use ambient/Common Magic as an intermediary between disciplines. She will use public records, old works and archived accounts and report to Gloin first. The research has not yet begun; do not involve Hadrik without Gloin's choice. ## Immediate family — Hammerfeld The Hammerfelds are a common-born working family in Karak-Varn, not wealthy or politically influential. Both parents are alive. Gloin is one of four children. Family members have their own work, concerns and relationships; they do not exist solely to support Gloin. ### Durgan Hammerfeld — 168 Gloin's father. Ironworker and repair smith. Gruff, practical, stubborn and quietly dependable. Measures people by their work and whether they keep their word. Loves Gloin but rarely says so directly. Respects his curiosity while worrying that he gets involved in matters beyond his experience. ### Mara Hammerfeld — 161 Gloin's mother. Runs the household and works part-time as a textile mender and clothing repairer. Warm, perceptive and sharp-tongued when needed; difficult to fool. Affectionate but no pushover. Notices when something troubles Gloin and is likely to challenge him about sleeping rough while family is nearby. ### Bruni Hammerfeld — 57 Gloin's older sister. Apprentice armourer working toward becoming a full craftswoman. Competitive, confident, blunt, ambitious and fiercely protective beneath her teasing. She remembers Gloin as an inquisitive nuisance and gives him grief for disappearing from family life. Offers practical fabrication, armour and metallurgy help. ### Tovin Hammerfeld — 34 Gloin's younger brother. Mine maintenance worker specialising in pumps, drainage and ventilation. Sociable, good-humoured, impulsive, mechanically minded and sometimes impatient. He and Gloin share a friendly rivalry; Tovin admires Gloin's willingness to try new things but thinks he can take himself too seriously. Offers practical knowledge of pumps and ventilation. Continuity correction: Tovin is Gloin's younger brother. Their canonical ages are Gloin 42 and Tovin 34 from the campaign's beginning on Autumn Day 19; Tovin is younger. The earlier age entry is a corrected source error, not an in-world age change. ### Elska Hammerfeld — 26 Gloin's youngest sister. Errand-runner and junior clerk at a local merchant's counting house. Clever, observant, curious, quietly mischievous and a good listener. Looks up to Gloin more than she admits. She has agreed to conduct discreet research for him into historical uses of ambient/Common Magic as an intermediary between disciplines. ## Extended family — Coppervein ### Harn Coppervein — 174 Gloin's maternal uncle and Mara's older brother. Retired stonecutter who takes occasional measuring and repair jobs. Patient, dry-humoured and opinionated about workmanship. Treats Gloin as capable of more than he gives himself credit for, but expects him to prove it. ### Vessa Coppervein — 158 Harn's wife. Baker attached to a neighbourhood provisions shop. Sociable, practical, generous with food and an enthusiastic collector of local gossip. Fond of Gloin. ### Rurik Coppervein — 39 Harn and Vessa's son; Gloin's cousin. Cartwright's assistant. Easygoing, competitive and fond of joking at Gloin's expense. They grew up seeing one another regularly, though work and adulthood have made visits less frequent. ## Teachers, mentors and scholarly contacts ### Maela Deepforge — 143 Khazari master runesmith and architectural historian. Silver-grey hair tightly braided back with small metal rings in the braids. Runs The Silver Anvil in the Upper Artisan Quarter. Expert in ancient runic construction, containment architecture, magical materials and runesmithing. Blunt, practical, respected and no-nonsense, with occasional dry humour. She is Gloin's provisional runesmithing teacher and the specialist contracted for the eastern mine inspection. She accepted Veyron's inspection contract under conditions recorded in the campaign record. Maela is discreet and politically aware. She distinguishes observed evidence from interpretation, is careful not to overstate magical conclusions and does not disclose sensitive mine findings to people who have not been told. ### Borin Ashmantle Older Khazari with a grey beard and two missing fingers on his left hand. Former mining engineer and apprentice during the original eastern mine sealing. Childhood acquaintance of Gloin; practical, cautious, protective and loyal. Borin retains the original partial survey hidden at his home. He teaches Gloin engineering fundamentals: structural weaknesses, tunnel safety, supports, airflow, seepage, tools and surveying. He has not committed to entering the mine. He remembers Thrain's wrapped iron object and the unidentified fourth official from the original sealing. ### Hadrik Ironvein — approximately 176 Khazari scholar and senior researcher at the Royal Historical Archive. Has worked there for 112 years and studied First Throne history for roughly 40 years. Careful and intellectually honest, loyal to Khazari people and history but not blindly loyal to the Crown. Research into First Throne history was administratively restricted about 40 years ago. Lent Gloin The Foundations of First Throne Script. Investigating the private repository and an obscured access-register name. Hadrik believes the First Throne may have been escaping something beneath its civilisation, but has no definitive answer. ### Sergeant Keldrun Broadshield — approximately 187 Veteran Khazari infantryman with more than a century of military experience. Specialises in shield fighting, one-handed axes and hammers, formation combat, confined tunnels and defence against larger opponents. Teaches at The Iron Circle. Has accepted Gloin into a six-week civilian course. His initial assessment found promising instincts for balance and redirection, footwork needing refinement, fair axe control, untested power and good discipline. ## Historical and mine-related contacts ### Edda Coppervein Older female dwarf and granddaughter of Thrain Coppervein. Lives in the Lower Artisan District. Keeps Thrain's old possessions and the original parchment note attributed to him. Allowed Gloin to copy the note; the original remains with the family. Remembers family stories about Thrain's missing iron object and his disagreement with Orik. ### Edrik Voss — approximately 60 Deputy Examiner of the Royal Mining Office. Black trimmed beard, scar from right ear to jaw, silver royal mining signet. Sought Borin's original survey and threatened him during their encounter. Edrik said the western wall was breached 11 nights before Autumn Day 19, watchmen heard three knocks and voices they did not understand, and “something came through”. He said the Crown wanted the matter contained and that King Durgan had not been informed, with the investigation handled under Veyron. His intentions and the accuracy of his claims remain unresolved. ### Lord Chancellor Veyron Senior political official. His office ordered restricted historical reviews and commissioned Maela's mine inspection. According to Edrik, the Royal Mining Office is acting under Veyron's authority. Veyron's motives and the King's knowledge remain unresolved; no conspiracy is established. ### Captain Roderic Vale Commander of the royal security detail assigned to Maela's inspection. Maela has not worked with him and does not know his purpose beyond command of the security detail. Further character details are unknown. ## Eastern mine inspection personnel ### Rennik Varn Eastern mine site supervisor. Responsible for the inspection site and its schedule. Can be defensive or irritated when procedures disrupt his work, but prioritises the site schedule. Knows official maintenance reports; do not assume he knows restricted ancient history or has malicious intent. ### Feldin Structural assessor. Stocky dwarf with a closely trimmed brown beard. Practical, experienced and friendly. Identifies structural distinctions and possible altered masonry, but is careful not to call an uncertain feature a doorway or hidden chamber without evidence. ### Orsa Resonance and material assessor. Thinner dwarf who carries a leather instrument case. Methodical and honest about the limits of the instruments. Uses a brass resonance gauge and can record changes, but cannot by itself identify whether a source is magical, mechanical or geological. ### Darrik Stonehand Off-duty watchman. Broad-shouldered, weathered face, dark beard streaked with grey. Independently reported three irregular knocks beyond the western boundary wall, faint whispering without words, brief scraping and a cold patch near old boundary markers. Did not hear the low hum reported by Harnel. ### Harnel Darrik's watch partner. Heard the three irregular knocks beyond the western wall, but no voices. Independently recalled faint scraping, a cold draught near the markers, a low hum lasting roughly three to four seconds after checking the wall, and a thin line of dust near the markers the following morning. He did not report a pile of dust. Served watches for 11 years and had not heard similar knocks. ## Other established or mentioned contacts ### Thuldren Maela's first Deepcraft instructor. Maela studied architecture, stonework and Runecraft before learning Deepcraft from him. He taught her to distinguish sensing from understanding. Further details are not established. ## Relationships and knowledge boundaries - The Hammerfeld family learned the mine and First Throne details because Gloin disclosed them during the Day 21 family supper. Other characters do not know those details unless they were separately told or could reasonably discover them. - Maela is discreet and does not reveal sensitive mine findings in front of people who do not know them. - Elska's ambient/Common Magic research is separate from Hadrik's historical repository work. Gloin does not want Hadrik involved in Elska's task unless he later chooses otherwise. - Darrik and Harnel gave separate accounts before comparing details. Preserve the differences between what each heard. - Hadrik's beliefs about the First Throne are interpretations, not secret knowledge of what lies behind the eastern mine door. - NPCs may have information unknown to Gloin, but the narrator must establish a plausible source before revealing it. ## Open biographical details Do not invent the following without developing them in play: - Exact ages, family histories or physical appearances not recorded above. - Full family finances, debts, home address or property ownership. - Any further biographical details about Tovin and Gloin not yet established. - Hadrik's final repository findings and the identity of the obscured register name. - Veyron's motives or the King's actual knowledge. - Captain Roderic Vale's personal background or reasons for assignment. - Thuldren's later life, current location or other students.
